title: How to Use Switch Statements in Javascript
summary: Introduces the switch statement as a tidier alternative to a long if-else chain, then uses it to map each drum button's letter to a different sound file.

concepts.heading: Why switch
points: With seven possible letters, an if / else if chain would be long and repetitive. A switch picks one branch based on the value of a single expression.
Editors can autocomplete the switch skeleton when you type the keyword.

concepts.heading: Switch syntax
points: switch (expression) { ... } evaluates the expression once; here it is a variable holding the clicked button's text.
Store the value first: var buttonInnerHTML = this.innerHTML; this is the button that fired the listener.
Each case label is followed by a colon and the statements to run when the value matches (a strict comparison against the case value).
break ends the case and exits the switch so execution carries on after it. Without it, execution would fall through into the next case.
default is the catch-all, like a final else. It handles values no case matched, such as an unexpected character.
Even if default seems unreachable, include it; here it just logs the unexpected value, which helps debugging later.

concepts.heading: Applying it to the drum kit
points: Cases: w plays tom-1, a tom-2, s tom-3, d tom-4, j snare, k crash, l kick-bass (these match the images chosen in the previous lesson).
Name each Audio variable after its sound (tom1, tom2, snare...) rather than reusing the name audio, and call play() on the same variable you created.
After saving, each button now plays a different sound.
Next lesson adds keyboard events so keys trigger the same sounds.

pitfalls: Forgetting break, so execution falls through and runs the next case's code too.
Mismatch between the variable declared in a case and the one on which play() is called (e.g. tom1 declared but audio.play()).
Case values are strings, so the letters need quotes and match case-sensitively.
(Extra) The sound files tom-2.mp3 etc. exist in the course starter's sounds folder; the reference lesson 18.03 folder includes only tom-1.mp3, while 18.04 has the full set.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (section 18 has no playground file).
gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson 'Switch statements': tasks: (1) convert a three-branch if/else chain to switch, (2) add a default that logs, (3) remove a break and observe fall-through, (4) group two cases sharing a result, (5) map drum letters to sound names.
Interactive demo: type a letter and highlight the case that matches in a rendered switch, with a toggle to remove break.
